name: blade-ai-v0.7.4
body:
## blade-ai blade-ai-v0.7.4

Bundles ChaosBlade tool v1.9.0-alpha for Linux / macOS,
plus the built-in Web UI — `blade-ai web` serves the console from the
standalone binary with no extra install.
The Windows client ships without the blade binary (no upstream
Windows agent) — injection there runs through kubectl-native
control-plane faults, `kubectl exec` into cluster tool pods, and
remote ssh/kubewiz host transports. `kubectl.exe` on PATH is the
only local prerequisite.

### Installation

**macOS / Linux:**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://chaosblade.io/install-agent.sh | bash
```

**Specify version:**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://chaosblade.io/install-agent.sh | bash -s -- --version 0.7.4
```

**Windows (PowerShell):**
```powershell
irm https://chaosblade.io/install-agent.ps1 | iex
```

### 🌐 OSS Download Links
Alternative download links from Alibaba Cloud OSS (faster in mainland China):

- [blade-ai-linux-amd64.tar.gz](https://chaosblade.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/blade-ai/github/blade-ai-v0.7.4/blade-ai-linux-amd64.tar.gz)
- [blade-ai-linux-arm64.tar.gz](https://chaosblade.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/blade-ai/github/blade-ai-v0.7.4/blade-ai-linux-arm64.tar.gz)
- [blade-ai-darwin-amd64.tar.gz](https://chaosblade.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/blade-ai/github/blade-ai-v0.7.4/blade-ai-darwin-amd64.tar.gz)
- [blade-ai-darwin-arm64.tar.gz](https://chaosblade.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/blade-ai/github/blade-ai-v0.7.4/blade-ai-darwin-arm64.tar.gz)
- [blade-ai-windows-x64.zip](https://chaosblade.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/blade-ai/github/blade-ai-v0.7.4/blade-ai-windows-x64.zip)
- [checksums.txt](https://chaosblade.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/blade-ai/github/blade-ai-v0.7.4/checksums.txt) - SHA256 checksums

**Install from the OSS mirror:**
```bash
curl -fsSL https://chaosblade.io/install-agent.sh | \
  BLADE_AI_MIRROR=https://chaosblade.oss-cn-hangzhou.aliyuncs.com/blade-ai/github \
  bash -s -- --version 0.7.4
```

Verify the download via `checksums.txt` before extracting.


## What's Changed

This release is a systematic pass over the **trustworthiness of the verification path**, the **way the skill library is loaded**, and the **unification of the transport layer**, plus a large expansion of the fault-case catalogue.

### Added
- **Typed HTTP probe tools**: added two read-only probe tools, `http_probe` / `host_http_probe`. Previously, observing an L7 HTTP fault (status-code tampering, latency, connection loss) during the verify / recover-verify phases required the model to hand-write a `curl` command, which was easily rejected by the read-only screen (e.g. `curl -D` writes a local file), and whose hand-written `-w` output the metric extractor could not parse — so key metrics like `http_code` and `time_connect` never entered the observation timeline. The probes now issue a typed request from an **independent client**, avoiding the false `exit 28` caused by kube-proxy hairpin, and make the metrics collectible by the deterministic cross-check.
- **Dual-root skill loading**: the read-only built-in skill pack is now **merge-loaded in place** alongside the writable user root, instead of being copied into the user directory on first run. The old copy never refreshed and, being same-named, shadowed the fresh built-in cases. When a genuine multi-root merge happens, the TUI's `skills reload` / `skills path` now list every root, so a redirected `skills_dir` no longer hides where the built-in cases come from.
- **Four transport channel implementations**: kubeconfig, kubewiz-k8s, kubewiz-host and SSH, unified behind a single-authority `TransportChannel` seam.
- **Target identity and postmortem**: added the `target_identity` and postmortem modules, together with a task-state single source and a metric extractor.
- **CLI preflight diagnostics**: added preflight diagnostics and completed the runner / recover-stream interrupt-recovery handling.
- **k8s_native provider**: added the `_argv` / `_fixes` assembly seams.
- **Large expansion of the fault-case catalogue**: added host network faults (DNS unavailable, packet loss/duplicate/corrupt/reorder, latency, bandwidth throttling) and a batch of Kubernetes case families (CronJob, Pod HTTP, Secret, ServiceAccount permissions, StatefulSet rolling, Webhook admission, plus Pending LimitRange misconfiguration, silent disk-IO tampering, inode exhaustion, eviction by higher-priority preemption, image-pull timeout, and PDB-blocked drain).

### Changed
- **Execute/verify node pipeline** reworked around effect probes: the effect-probe form replaces the former `_effect_channels` / `_effect_checks`.
- **Target guard** extended with classifier and mechanism-write checks, plus a read-only-probe exemption for host injection.
- **Memory**: reworked the session finalizer and added hook evidence-fingerprint and turn-accumulator-funnel metric extraction.
- **Server**: tidied the turn / event-stream / skills routes and added inject-connection state isolation.
- **Hardened read-only command surface**: read-only screening, guard, host_cmd, kubectl_cli and progress reporting tightened together.

### Fixed
- Fixed the verify phase hand-writing a `curl` that got falsely rejected by the read-only screen, dragging legitimate sibling reads in the same batch down with it and burning a whole verify iteration.
- Fixed the built-in skill pack's stale copy shadowing the fresh cases, which kept the skill library from ever refreshing.

### Chore
- Coordinated the version to **0.7.4** (pyproject.toml, uv.lock, package-lock.json, tui/web package.json, and `__init__.py`).

**Full Changelog**: v1.8.2...blade-ai-v0.7.4


**Full Changelog**: https://github.com/chaosblade-io/chaosblade/compare/v1.8.2...blade-ai-v0.7.4

  bash -s -- --version 0.7.1
```

Verify the download via `checksums.txt` before extracting.


## What's Changed

### 🚀 New Features

- **FaultDrill CR channel** — a new declarative fault carrier: the fault is a single `FaultDrill` CustomResource, `kubectl apply` is the injection, controller-style reconciliation of `spec.restorePatches` is the recovery, and the TTL reads `status.injectedAt` (cluster state, so recovery survives agent death). The CRD is installed lazily with a schema-compatibility check, and every unavailability path (RBAC denial, incompatible CRD, admission policy) is a *routing* signal that degrades to the existing recovery-carrier SOP — never a task failure. Credentials stay out of the CR: `invalidSecret` carries a source reference plus transformation recipe, never inlined material.

- **Fault-window hold with in-turn recovery** (opt-in, off by default; turn channel only — CLI/SDK behaviour is unchanged)

  **Behaviour**: when enabled, a turn is no longer finalized as soon as injection verification completes — it holds through the injection contract window. The window is computed as *injection effective time + injection duration*, presented as remaining time from the verifier entry; verification and hold time both count against the same contract window and never extend the fault's lifetime. During the hold the SSE stream carries `fault_window` events (enter / tick / exit): a 25-second tick both re-syncs the client's local countdown against clock drift and keeps intermediate proxies from closing an idle connection.

  **Interaction**: the TUI shows a rotating spinner with a live countdown (`fault window in progress · 4m30s left · ctrl+r recover now · esc exit`), taking over the regular loading-indicator slot (single-spinner mutex). At window expiry — or early via **Ctrl+R** (`POST /api/v1/sessions/{sid}/turns/{turn_id}/early-recover`) — the recovery graph is dispatched *within the same turn*: destroy, recovery verification and the result report all stream live, so the full fault lifecycle closes inside one SSE connection with no extra recover request to issue.

  **Safety boundary**: pressing ESC during the hold (client disconnect) only ends the live stream — fault recovery is still backed by the existing blade timeout and carrier timers, with no new leak surface.

  **Scope**: single-fault inject dispatches only. Batch dispatches are excluded — each fault in a batch carries its own contract window, so there is no single window to hold.

  **How to enable** (a hot key — effective after `settings.reload()` with no restart; the next turn picks up the new value. `turn_hold_fault_window` is in the `/api/v1/config` write whitelist, and the string `"true"` is auto-cast to boolean). Any one of:

  - CLI: `blade-ai config set turn_hold_fault_window true`
  - TUI slash command: `/config set turn_hold_fault_window true`
  - HTTP API: `POST /api/v1/config/turn_hold_fault_window` with body `{"value": "true"}` (the response carries `hot_reload: true`)
  - Config file: `"turn_hold_fault_window": true` in `~/.blade-ai/config.json`
  - Environment variable: `BLADE_AI_TURN_HOLD_FAULT_WINDOW=true`

  **To disable**: `/config unset turn_hold_fault_window` or `DELETE /api/v1/config/turn_hold_fault_window`.

- **Session resume** — `blade-ai resume` (bare form lists resumable sessions, `-i <sid>` takes over) plus `/resume` in the frontends. History is rebuilt from the session's events jsonl through the *same* `StreamEvent → Action` mapping the live SSE path uses, so a replayed session cannot drift from a live one. The CLI picker and the TUI list share one source of truth (`GET /api/v1/memory/resumable`); when the events file is missing there is deliberately no fallback chain.

- **Third verdict: `unverified`** — verification can now conclude "cannot tell" instead of claiming a failure nobody observed. Injection verdicts are `verified` / `partial` / `unverified` and render as `✓` / `◐` / `?` in batch summaries; recovery mirrors it with `recovered` / `partial_recovered` / `unverified` / `failed`, where `unverified` is explicitly *not* a recovery failure (the destroy may well have succeeded — restore observability and re-confirm) and keeps the task in the recoverable set. Results now carry an `observation_failures` list classifying each failed probe as `auth` / `transient` / `unknown`.

- **Create-reconcile gate** — a create whose transport timed out or failed with a transient no-UID error is reconciled against the live cluster before any retry. The gate fingerprints the original request (namespace / labels / target names / scope) and only releases on a whitelisted read or a completed probe, so a non-idempotent create can no longer silently duplicate a fault on the same target.

- **Write-set boundary** — the skill case file's `mechanism_writes` manifest is parsed deterministically (invisible to the model), rendered verbatim in the confirmation card as **"Writes beyond victim — approving authorizes these cluster writes"**, frozen into the approved target, and enforced fail-closed by the drift guard beyond the manifest's name union. Unattended channels share one boundary decision: a widened contract auto-approves with an auditable `auto_approved` event carrying the entries.

- **Deterministic verdict rules** — a new Layer 1.5 in the verification chain turns measured numbers into a verdict without an LLM adjudication round whenever the comparison is decidable.

- **Intent anchor** — the target the user explicitly named is pinned up front, so probe ordering can no longer lock a different scope/labels contract and trigger spurious drift rejections.

- **Carrier image discovery is now self-healing** — the DaemonSet-image probe retries (two attempts with backoff), a starved discovery set gets an execute-time refresh (bounded to once per process) before classification, discovered healthy images merge back into settings for reuse, and the set is deduped and sorted.

### 🛡️ Reliability & Correctness

- **Transient failure retries**: transport-level classification of dispatch failures (`No executor available for cluster`, stale executor heartbeat) with bounded backoff — the command never reached an executor, so retrying is semantically safe — plus an exception-type retry for idempotent LLM call sites.
- **Tool-pairing integrity**: a single gate on outbound message lists repairs orphaned or mismatched `tool` messages before send, closing the 400s strict providers returned on sequences lenient ones accepted silently.
- **Verdict vocabulary is a closed set**: both write and read paths clamp any out-of-vocabulary level to the domain's fail-closed word and warn, so legacy or foreign words can no longer masquerade as a real verdict.
- **One read-only classifier**: the three divergent "is this a read-only probe?" vocabularies (injection attribution, guard scope, tool screening) are unified into a single source of truth.
- **Execution artifacts index**: debug-pod identity and other side effects discovered from executed tool results are recorded durably instead of being re-inferred from prose by safety and recovery code.
- **Truncation contract**: everything truncated into the model's context now carries a machine-parseable marker, an honestly reported original size, and a retrieval path (or an explicit whitelisted omission).
- **Kubeconfig resolution** moved into a single graph-wide contract, so settlement primitives can no longer re-home a destroy onto the wrong cluster by reading a bare state key.
- **Abort semantics unified**: whichever mechanism wins the race (scope cancel, disconnect poll, internal error) now converges on the same stream-terminal record.
- **Task ledger**: rows track which experiments a task still owns, which it retired, and whether a native mutation was issued; the boot card splits pending rows into **In flight / Awaiting recovery / Completed but uncleared**.
- **MCP effect labels**: a server-declared destructive tool is never silently presented as read-only — the label is surfaced in the tool description and recorded in the connect log.

### 🖥️ TUI

- Fault-window indicator with live countdown, taking over the spinner slot for the duration of the hold.
- Terminal-level attention signals (bell / notification escape sequences) when a confirmation gate fires while you are in another window — deliberately silenced while a replay is being watched.
- Boot cards shared between fresh boot and resume boot, so both surfaces stay at visual parity; resume-argv parsing and a cache-hit-rate indicator beside the context gauge.

### 🌐 Web UI

- Context-window meter and cache-hit rate in the status bar, mirroring the TUI's formatting semantics over the same shared store fields.
- Confirmation card updated for the widened write-set contract; trace page and info cards refined.

### 📚 Docs, Skills & Knowledge

- README documents the `unverified` verdict and the per-fault-type default timeout floor (300 s when no duration is stated; an explicitly stated duration is honored verbatim).
- New environment fact files: recovery carrier, host timer channel, node cached images; new knowledge entry on outcome-to-means methodology.
- New drill-case catalogues (ConfigMap content tampering, node unavailable via kubelet stop, Pod Pending from ResourceQuota / unbound STS PVC, Pod network packet reordering) and a case-drill log template.

### 🔧 Build & Upgrade

- Version bumped to 0.7.1 across `pyproject.toml`, core, tui and web.
- Existing task databases gain the new ledger columns automatically — the startup migrations are idempotent additive `ALTER TABLE` steps on both SQLite and PostgreSQL, so no manual action is needed. (If you are coming from a pre-0.6.10 database, the manual rename noted in that release still applies.)
- Packaging spec comments updated: the Windows binary is informational/TUI-only.

```

## What's Changed

### ✨ Features

**Progress Ledger & Agent Pipeline**

- Introduce the **progress ledger**: a model-maintained, three-layer working note (frozen anchor / current state / capped milestone log) written via the new `update_progress` tool. The executor stays anchored to its original goal across long runs, and the intent graph keeps visibility even when a turn is interrupted
- Strengthen planning: richer intent clarification and screening, plan-change validation, and a tool screener with description budget
- Harden execution: execute/agent loop rework, debug pod discovery and ephemeral container cleanup, reject-turn visibility and dialogue persistence
- Improved verifier/recover layers, operation summary, target guard vehicle-exec exemption and drift policy
- Richer L4 event stream: tool error events, connection-state fields, explicit channel / KubeWiz gateway fields
- Stronger tool guards: kubectl and readonly dual-use guards, host command adjustments; session store and tool compactor fixes

**CLI Lifecycle Rework**

- **Manifest-free uninstall**: uninstall now derives paths from install conventions (`~/.blade-ai/versions`, `~/.local/bin/blade-ai` symlink) instead of a fragile install manifest that went stale after updates — uninstall works reliably no matter how many times you've updated
- Reworked `update` command alongside the new layout
- Renamed `blade-ai serve` → `blade-ai server` for consistency with `blade-ai-server`

**TUI**

- Improved confirmation flow (batch fault intent preview), session memory card placeholders, and stream-disconnect reason surfacing
- New en/zh i18n strings; introduced ESLint tooling for the TUI codebase

- Makefile build/wheel targets now fail fast (`set -e`) instead of continuing silently after a vendor download failure

body:
This is the first version of chaosblade.  

# Features

Support the following chaos experiment:

* CPU full load
* Network package delay
* Network package block(drop)
* Network package loss
* DNS not available
* Fill disk
* Burn disk IO (include read and write)
* Kill process
* Delete pod
* Remove container
* Request delay, exception and timeout for Dubbo, Servlet, MySQL Driver component
* Java method invoked delay, exception or return the specified value

Exclude delete pod and remove container，the above chaos experiment can be executed in the container. 

Linux/amd64 and darwin/amd64 versions are available, but some network and disk experiments cannot be executed in darwin/amd64 version.
